page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), alongside hardware-assisted cryptography. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth scaling. The instance achieved average tier results in single-core stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, multi-core performance falls into the bottom quartile, as seen in the Geekbench multi-core score of 4154.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 3219.87. Memory bandwidth is also in the bottom quartile, measuring 33.17 GB/sec for large-block reads and 21.19 GB/sec for large-block writes. Cryptographic performance remains moderate with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 3426.33, and static web serving throughput is stable at 7.0 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio within a budget-friendly hardware class, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel processing or high memory bandwidth. Given the weak multi-core scaling and low database operation scores, this instance is best suited for lightweight caching layers, single-threaded applications, text processing, basic web serving, and small-scale memory-intensive tasks rather than heavy database hosting or complex parallel compilations.
